why: P3 because it fixes a real but narrow correctness bug: FillPSBT could fail to sign an owned input when a PSBT coordinator supplies conflicting witness_utxo and non_witness_utxo.
The failure mode is a stuck/incomplete signature, not fund loss or a wrong signature, so it is a reliability fix rather than a fund-safety one.
Comes with regression tests pinning both the GetUTXO prefer/reject rules and the FillPSBT behavior.

result.summary: Fixes FillPSBT in the wallet so it selects the SigningProvider using the same GetUTXO prefer/reject rule that SignPSBTInput already uses, instead of preferring witness_utxo unconditionally. Previously, if a PSBT's witness_utxo and non_witness_utxo disagreed, FillPSBT could pick keys for the wrong script and fail to complete a signature for an input the wallet actually owns. The PR adds a psbt.h doc comment clarifying GetUTXO's prefer/reject semantics, a unit test pinning those semantics, and a wallet regression test for the fix.
result.problem: A PSBT input can carry both non_witness_utxo and witness_utxo; when they disagree (e.g. a malicious or buggy PSBT coordinator tampers with witness_utxo), FillPSBT previously chose the wrong script for key/signing-provider selection while SignPSBTInput used a different rule, causing signing to fail even though the wallet owned the appropriate input. This affects wallet users completing PSBTs with an external or mutated coordinator input.

result.card: This PR fixes a wallet bug where FillPSBT could fail to sign a PSBT input the wallet actually owns, when the input's non_witness_utxo and witness_utxo disagree, by routing FillPSBT's script/key selection through the same GetUTXO prefer/reject rule SignPSBTInput already uses. The problem, per the description, is that 'FillPSBT loaded keys for the witness_utxo script while SignPSBTInput signed the non_witness_utxo spend,' producing an incomplete signature even though the wallet holds the right key; the author clarifies the risk is failure-to-sign, not signing the wrong UTXO. The PR adds a regression test and a GetUTXO-semantics unit test. One reviewer (vicjuma) questioned the motivation and threat model; the author gave a concrete malicious/buggy-coordinator explanation and received no further pushback, so the concern reads as resolved. The PR is labeled Needs rebase, so a review now may need to be redone after rebase. No stated dependencies or blockers beyond that.
